items.title: 61124_Mario Bauza oral history interview
items.q: The same thing that happen when Tito Puente I brought (inaudible) to the band. Chano (inaudible) got (inaudible) and got a hold of Tito Tico Puente. I said, teach him how to play the BAILA paya (phonetic), teach him how to do like this, to play the cowbell.

ctx.x: discovered everything, that they knew. The last time I I couldn't find nobody (inaudible) to play a rhythm (inaudible). That little (inaudible) Machito's band in the beginning had to be taught to people. I don't have for three months. I've been (inaudible) for three months. He ain't got no idea what I went through. Now the scene is different. Everybody play. Or they do this, they think they play. (Inaudible). But there nobody play.

So when Chico Tiko left (inaudible) McGuire and some hinky-dink (inaudible). At least he got that thing, you know. He got that frame. (inaudible). The same thing that happen when Tito Puente I brought (inaudible) to the band. Chano (inaudible) got (inaudible) and got a hold of Tito Tico Puente. I said, teach him how to play the BAILA paya (phonetic), teach him how to do like this, to play the cowbell. (Inaudible) that kind of stuff.
Now, I hear people talk about the (inaudible). No, no. He learned that here, right in my band.
